description: Phase 5: Feed Recommendation Engine - Implement a modular signal-based recommendation system in the backend. Add getUserFeedSignals() function, implement 80/20 preference-matched vs discovery split, store configurable weights in AppConfig, add artworkType index to Post model. Users without interests get the current algorithm unchanged. No Admin Panel UI for weights.
steps: 1. In backend/src/modules/posts/post.model.js, add an index on artworkType: postSchema.index({ artworkType: 1 }); (after the existing tags index). This optimizes queries filtering by artwork type for the recommendation engine.

2. Create a new file backend/src/modules/posts/recommendation.service.js. This module implements the signal aggregation layer with the following exports: (a) getUserFeedSignals(userId) - fetches user's interests from User model, returns a structured signals object; (b) getRecommendationWeights() - fetches weights from AppConfig (key: 'feed_recommendation_weights'), returns defaults if not set; (c) buildRecommendedFeed(userId, cursor, limit, showMatureContent) - the main recommendation function that implements the 80/20 split.

3. In recommendation.service.js, implement getUserFeedSignals(userId): Fetch the user document, extract interests array, return { interestSignals: user.interests || [], hasPreferences: (user.interests && user.interests.length > 0) }. This is designed to be extensible - future signals (follow graph, interaction history) can be added to this return object without restructuring.

4. In recommendation.service.js, implement getRecommendationWeights(): Query AppConfig.findOne({ key: 'feed_recommendation_weights' }). If found, return config.value. If not found, return sensible defaults: { preferenceWeight: 0.8, discoveryWeight: 0.2, popularityLikeMultiplier: 3, popularitySaveMultiplier: 5, recencyBoostHours: 48 }.

5. In recommendation.service.js, implement buildRecommendedFeed(userId, cursor, limit, showMatureContent): (a) Call getUserFeedSignals(userId); (b) If !signals.hasPreferences, return null (caller falls back to existing algorithm); (c) If hasPreferences: fetch posts matching artworkType filter (using $in with interestSignals) for 80% of limit slots, fetch remaining 20% from non-matching posts for discovery; (d) Apply popularity scoring from weights; (e) Return combined and sorted results with cursor pagination.

6. In backend/src/modules/posts/post.service.js, modify the getFeed function: Before the existing algorithm, attempt to use the recommendation engine. Import buildRecommendedFeed from './recommendation.service.js'. At the start of getFeed, if userId is provided, call buildRecommendedFeed(userId, cursor, limit, showMatureContent). If it returns a non-null result, use that. If it returns null (user has no preferences), fall through to the existing algorithm unchanged.

7. Ensure backward compatibility: The existing getFeed algorithm remains the complete fallback. The recommendation engine only activates when: (a) user is authenticated AND (b) user has interests set. All existing feed behavior for guests and users without preferences is unchanged.

8. In the recommendation.service.js buildRecommendedFeed function, apply the same safety filters as the existing getFeed: exclude soft-deleted posts (deletedAt: null), exclude posts from banned/suspended users, apply NSFW filtering based on showMatureContent parameter.
acceptance_criteria: Post model has index on artworkType field
recommendation.service.js exists with getUserFeedSignals, getRecommendationWeights, and buildRecommendedFeed exports
getUserFeedSignals returns structured signals object with user interests
getRecommendationWeights reads from AppConfig with sensible defaults as fallback
buildRecommendedFeed implements 80/20 split between preference-matched and discovery posts
buildRecommendedFeed returns null when user has no preferences (triggering fallback)
post.service.js getFeed integrates recommendation engine with graceful fallback
Existing feed algorithm is unchanged for guests and users without interests
All safety filters applied: deletedAt null, inactive users excluded, NSFW filtering
No Admin Panel UI added for weights configuration
Signal aggregator is modular - new signals can be added without restructuring
Weights stored in AppConfig with key 'feed_recommendation_weights'
verification: Read post.model.js and confirm artworkType index exists
Read recommendation.service.js and confirm all three exported functions exist with correct logic
Read post.service.js getFeed and confirm it calls buildRecommendedFeed with proper fallback
Verify recommendation.service.js applies safety filters (deletedAt, inactive users, NSFW)
